subject.title: [Bug]: Agents should not be able to access or modify files outside their own working space.

question: What default filesystem boundary should host-based agents get, and how should existing trusted host-wide access migrate or opt out?
rationale: The report is source-reproducible and security-sensitive, but the fix changes default tool access, compatibility expectations, and the boundary between file tools, exec, and sandbox backends.

options.title: Keep open for staged security fix
options.body: Use this issue as the concrete bug anchor while maintainers review focused containment PRs and decide the broader default and migration model.

options.title: Adopt workspace-only by default
options.body: Switch file tools to workspace-only by default and provide an explicit documented escape hatch for trusted host workflows.

options.title: Route to sandbox-only guidance
options.body: Document Docker, SSH, or OpenShell sandboxing as the required hard boundary and leave host file tools permissive by default.

recommendation.title: Keep open for staged security fix
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the concrete bug anchor while maintainers review focused containment PRs and decide the broader default and migration model.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history signal for the workspace-only filesystem guard and has already framed this as a maintainer security/default decision.
